title: Fine-Scale Cavity Resonance Optimization with Frozen Outer Mirrors
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining optimization to the cavity region (layers 8-12) with ±2 nm perturbations around the R3 best candidate will reveal whether the score plateau at ~0.9757 is due to coarse step resolution or genuine physical limits; finer 0.25 nm steps may detect secondary resonance peaks from higher-order mode coupling.
design_principle: Freeze outer DBR mirror layers to preserve established stopband performance; apply high-resolution local optimization only to the central cavity block where resonance tuning most directly affects peak transmittance at 1550 nm.
proposed_topology: 21-layer symmetric Fabry-Perot: Air | [Ta2O5/SiO2]_6 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | [SiO2/Ta2O5]_6 | Fused Silica. Exact sequence: L1(Ta2O5), L2(SiO2), L3(Ta2O5), L4(SiO2), L5(Ta2O5), L6(SiO2), L7(Ta2O5), L8(SiO2), L9(Ta2O5), L10(SiO2), L11(Ta2O5), L12(SiO2), L13(Ta2O5), L14(SiO2), L15(Ta2O5), L16(SiO2), L17(Ta2O5), L18(SiO2), L19(Ta2O5), L20(SiO2), L21(Ta2O5).
design_variables: thicknesses of layers 8-12 with ±2 nm bounds around [113.01, 182.11, 253.25, 251.08, 301.44] nm
soft_objectives: minimize transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands
manufacturing_considerations: thickness control within ±2 nm feasible with quartz crystal monitoring
0.25 nm step resolution requires high-precision deposition equipment
theory_basis: Defective DBR bandpass filter principle: (HL)^N D(LH)^N structure creates transmission peak at defect mode wavelength
Needle optimization technique for non-quarter-wave thickness refinement in thin spectral regions
expected_advantages: Higher resolution may reveal score improvements beyond 0.9757 plateau
Frozen outer mirrors reduce optimization dimensionality and prevent stopband degradation
Focused cavity tuning directly targets the 1550 nm transmission peak
known_risks: Score may not improve if 0.9757 represents physical limit for 21-layer symmetric design
Over-constraining layers 8-12 may prevent discovery of better asymmetric cavity configurations
Fine step resolution increases computation time without guaranteed payoff
execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 Fabry-Perot bandpass filter on fused silica substrate for 1550 nm LiDAR receiver. Incident medium is air. Initialize from the R3 best candidate thicknesses: [173.25, 324.48, 150.60, 227.07, 188.79, 260.87, 173.64, 111.52, 113.01, 182.11, 253.25, 251.08, 301.44, 148.31, 404.39, 392.31, 167.99, 366.33, 206.82, 195.34, 248.81] nm. Freeze layers 1-7 and 13-21 at these values. Optimize only layers 8-12 with bounds ±2 nm around [111.52, 113.01, 182.11, 253.25, 251.08] nm respectively. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with minimum step resolution 0.25 nm. Evaluate coherent TMM transmittance spectrum from 1300-1800 nm at normal incidence, unpolarized. Score based on high transmission at 1550 nm and suppression in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Follows feedback directive to perform constrained local optimization on R3 top candidate with ±2 nm cavity bounds and 0.25 nm step resolution to test for fine-scale resonance improvements beyond 0.9757 plateau.
